positive.prompt: This codebase feels like spaghetti, one concept is spread over a dozen tiny files. Do an architecture review and tell me what to refactor first.
Do an architecture review of this repo and rank the refactoring candidates in a report
I cannot find where checkout logic lives, it bounces across many files. Review the architecture and rank the refactors.
Find the architectural friction in this project and show me before and after diagrams for the best candidates

negative.prompt: Review this diff before I merge it
Clean up this one function, it works but it is hard to follow
Plan the migration from the old billing API to the new one

evals.prompt: Do an architecture review of src/checkout. It feels over-split. Follow the improve-codebase-architecture process.
evals.expected_output: An HTML report written outside the repository with ranked deepening candidates that use the codebase-design vocabulary and the GLOSSARY.md terms, a deletion test result for each, no interfaces proposed, and a closing question asking which candidate to explore
expectations: A self-contained HTML file is written in the OS temp directory (or another path outside the project) and its absolute path is given to the user
No new file is added inside the project directory by the review itself
The report names the checkout files involved and gives at least one candidate that merges the small load, validate, stock, convert and save steps into a deeper Order placement module
Each candidate has a problem, a solution, benefits stated as locality or leverage, a before and after diagram, and a recommendation strength of Strong, Worth exploring or Speculative
The deletion test result is stated for the shallow modules under suspicion
The text uses the terms module, interface, seam, depth, leverage or locality, and avoids service, component, API and boundary as architecture words
The text uses the GLOSSARY.md terms (Order, Cart) and not the words purchase, transaction or basket
A candidate that would split the database is either absent or marked as contradicting ADR 0001 with a stated reason to reopen it
No new interface, signature or code for the deepened module is proposed in the report
The reply ends by asking which candidate the user wants to explore
